key_errors: cc1plus: error: /__w/openvino/openvino/openvino/openvino_build/src/core/reference/CMakeFiles/openvino_reference.dir/cmake_pch.hxx.gch: not a PCH file [-Werror=invalid-pch]
cc1plus: all warnings being treated as errors
root_cause: The ARM64 cross-compilation job's 'CMake configure, build and install - OpenVINO JS API' step reconfigures and rebuilds the SAME build directory already used for the main Release build (toggling TBB/wheel cache variables for the NPM/JS packaging pass) while -DCMAKE_COMPILE_WARNING_AS_ERROR=ON stays active. This forces a rebuild of openvino_reference, but the previously generated precompiled header object (cmake_pch.hxx.gch) under the reused CMakeFiles directory is now stale/incompatible for the reconfigured compiler invocation, so GCC's cc1plus rejects it with 'not a PCH file', and -Werror escalates this into a hard build failure for every reference op compiled in that pass. This is the same job-agnostic infrastructure defect already recorded 7 times against this workflow; the triggering commit (dependabot PR #38594, a flake8-bugbear version bump in src/bindings/python) is unrelated to the failure.
reproduction_steps: Not reliably reproducible outside CI without the exact ARM64 cross-compilation Docker image and cache state; locally: configure+build the main Release target in a build dir, then re-run 'cmake -UTBB* -S <repo> -B <same-build-dir> -DCPACK_GENERATOR=NPM -DENABLE_SYSTEM_TBB=OFF -DENABLE_WHEEL=OFF' followed by 'cmake --build <same-build-dir>' and observe cc1plus reject the cached src/core/reference/CMakeFiles/openvino_reference.dir/cmake_pch.hxx.gch as an invalid PCH file.
recommended_actions: Use a separate build directory for the JS/NPM cmake reconfigure instead of reusing BUILD_DIR, so the openvino_reference PCH is generated fresh for the new configuration
Explicitly remove/regenerate cmake_pch.hxx.gch (and other PCH artifacts) before or during the JS API cmake --build invocation in the ARM64 cross-compilation workflow step

Disable precompiled headers (ENABLE_FASTER_BUILD=OFF) for the JS/NPM reconfigure pass, or pass -DCMAKE_COMPILE_WARNING_AS_ERROR=OFF for that specific sub-build to avoid escalating stale-PCH warnings into hard failures

Escalate as a known, unresolved infrastructure issue against job_build_linux.yml for the ubuntu_22_arm64_cross_compilation workflow — this is now the 8th recorded occurrence since 2026-09-25 and remains unfixed
prevention_strategies: Avoid reconfiguring and rebuilding the same CMake build directory with different cache variables (TBB/wheel toggles for the JS/NPM pass) in sequential steps of the same job when precompiled headers are enabled; isolate the JS API packaging build into its own build directory, or explicitly invalidate PCH artifacts between reconfigures. Add a CI guard that detects 'not a PCH file' errors and automatically cleans stale .gch files before retrying.
historical_context: Identical failure signature recorded 7 times previously in this database: runs 36123294303 (2026-09-25), 37391757947, 37394029538, 37410819403, 37421582585, 37437000273, and 37440842108 (all 2026-10-06), all on the same 'Linux (Ubuntu 22.04, ARM64 cross-compilation, Python 3.11)' workflow with the same cc1plus invalid-pch cmake_pch.hxx.gch error during the JS API build pass. This is now the 8th occurrence; the defect in the shared build-directory PCH reuse remains unresolved and should be escalated as a persistent CI infra bug rather than investigated as a code regression each time.
